active_paradigms.idea: Replace the repeated SLSQP basin search with one high-accuracy interior-point solve using scipy.optimize.minimize(method="trust-constr") on the diameter-normalized formulation.
active_paradigms.description: The current program first produces spherical-code seeds by repulsion, then performs many SLSQP solves of the correct epigraph problem: maximize u subject to u <= d_ij^2 <= 1. This is strong because it directly matches the evaluator's squared ratio, fixes translation, supplies analytic first derivatives, and uses restarts to cross some contact-graph basins. Its main limitation is that SLSQP's active-set decisions and finite termination can leave a near-optimal configuration slightly inside or outside the true diameter/contact manifold; the observed 1.000016 score is consistent with a nearly correct known optimum rather than a clearly better geometry. Use scipy.optimize.minimize once with method="trust-constr", the same 39 coordinate variables plus u, exact lower and upper squared-distance constraints, and a scipy.optimize.NonlinearConstraint with the existing analytic Jacobian. Provide a Hessian update strategy such as BFGS or SR1, use very small barrier and optimality tolerances, and remove rotational null directions by fixing point 0 at the origin, point 1 on the x axis, and point 2 in the xy plane. Start from one deterministic high-quality seed rather than using the incumbent from a succession of optimizers. The interior-point trajectory can approach a degenerate active-contact solution more reliably than SLSQP, while the final u is exactly the evaluator metric after diameter normalization.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: The sole target is u=(dmin/dmax)^2. In particular, reduce numerical slack in simultaneously active minimum-distance and diameter constraints, since improvement over the reference is likely at the 1e-5 level.
active_paradigms.cautions: Do not maximize unsquared distance or constrain only a selected subset of pairs: all 91 lower and all 91 upper constraints must remain present. Gauge fixing must be implemented consistently in the variable unpacking and Jacobian. Return the coordinates and let the evaluator recompute distances; do not return the optimizer's u. trust-constr may need a realistic execution budget and sparse Jacobian representation to avoid timeout.

active_paradigms.idea: Solve the rigid active-contact equations directly with scipy.optimize.least_squares, using a fixed contact graph of the known 14-point diameter extremizer and KKT stationarity residuals.
active_paradigms.description: A qualitatively different route is to treat the best configuration as a tensegrity/contact-graph realization rather than as a generic inequality NLP. The current spherical repulsion plus SLSQP is good at discovering an approximate basin, but it does not exploit that at an optimum many pairs are exactly at the minimum distance or exactly at the diameter, and the remaining coordinates are determined to high precision by those equalities. Identify a fixed candidate contact graph from a trusted high-precision 14-point extremal configuration: label each edge as a short contact with d_ij^2=u or a diameter contact with d_ij^2=1. In one scipy.optimize.least_squares call, solve residuals consisting of these edge equations, translation/rotation gauge equations, and the KKT force-balance equations with nonnegative multipliers for the two edge classes. Include u, coordinates, and multipliers as variables, with bounds enforcing u>0 and nonnegative multipliers. The overdetermined residual system makes the geometric realization and its equilibrium self-stress much more stable than trying to infer active constraints afresh at every iterate. Evaluate all 91 distances afterward; if every noncontact distance lies strictly between u and 1, this produces a highly precise feasible candidate and can expose whether the reference's tiny excess is merely numerical. This directly targets the local algebraic optimum rather than attempting more random basins.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Numerical precision of the extremal contact geometry and verification that noncontact pairs do not become the true dmin or dmax. This is especially appropriate when the current score already nearly matches a known reference bound.
active_paradigms.cautions: This requires the contact graph to be correct; an incorrect graph can solve its equalities beautifully while violating an omitted pairwise bound. Do not derive the graph dynamically by running another optimizer inside the submitted function; hard-code a graph and a deterministic initial realization. Include enough gauge constraints to eliminate the six Euclidean rigid-motion degrees of freedom, and explicitly reject a result if any of all 91 distances violates its assigned interval.

active_paradigms.idea: Use scipy.optimize.differential_evolution as a single global search over a symmetry-reduced, smooth soft-extrema objective to seek a genuinely different contact graph.
active_paradigms.description: The present method's biggest global-search weakness is that all its seeds are spherical repulsion configurations and all subsequent moves are local SLSQP perturbations of one incumbent; this strongly favors the same spherical-code contact topology. Form a direct objective for scipy.optimize.differential_evolution over symmetry-reduced coordinates, fixing translation and rotation as point 0=(0,0,0), point 1=(x,0,0), and point 2=(a,b,0). For each candidate, center and scale it internally by its largest pairwise distance, then maximize a differentiable lower approximation to the minimum squared distance, for example a log-sum-exp soft minimum with a high inverse temperature over all 91 normalized squared distances. This normalization makes bounds on coordinates practical and exactly removes scale from the search objective. Use Sobol initialization, deterministic seed, workers=1, polish=False, and a population budget chosen for the timeout; this is a single global optimization call rather than a repulsion stage followed by local polishing. At the end, compute the exact hard min/max ratio only to select the returned member of the final population, not as a second optimization stage. Unlike an inequality solver, this approach can discover a different combinatorial contact graph whose actual hard ratio exceeds the apparent reference value.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Global exploration of contact-graph topology and the exact evaluator ratio, with the smooth surrogate used only to rank candidates during the one search call.
active_paradigms.cautions: A soft minimum can favor a candidate with many moderately short pairs instead of the best hard minimum; use a sufficiently sharp temperature and validate the exact ratio before return. Coordinate bounds must be broad enough not to exclude an equivalent realization, while gauge fixing avoids wasting dimensions on translations and rotations. Differential evolution can be expensive in 33-plus dimensions, so it is a topology-discovery alternative, not something to combine with the current repeated SLSQP pipeline.

tried_paradigms.idea: Replace stochastic basin hopping with a symmetry-reduced global search using scipy.optimize.differential_evolution
tried_paradigms.description: The current program first performs spherical inverse-power repulsion, then applies many SLSQP solves to the full 39-coordinate constrained problem. Its strength is the correct diameter-one formulation with analytic derivatives, which reaches the apparent reference contact graph; its principal weakness is that SLSQP is local and the many random perturbations mostly revisit the same basin. Instead, encode a plausible high-symmetry 14-point orbit construction with only a few geometric parameters, such as ring radii, heights, angular offsets, and any distinct orbit representatives under a chosen finite rotation/reflection group. Evaluate the true squared ratio directly after centering and scaling by the candidate diameter, so no separate scale variable or upper-distance constraints are needed. Call scipy.optimize.differential_evolution once on the bounded reduced parameter vector, with a fixed seed, Sobol initialization, polishing enabled, and tight tolerances. The optimizer should search several symmetry classes in separate program variants, rather than treating a single full-coordinate local optimum as evidence that its contact graph is globally best. This is especially promising because the score is already within numerical noise of the benchmark, so identifying the exact symmetry family can remove small asymmetries and expose a better contact configuration.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: The sole target is the evaluator's squared ratio (minimum pairwise squared distance divided by maximum pairwise squared distance). Reducing dimension makes global topology/contact-graph changes more likely than the current perturb-and-SLSQP schedule.
tried_paradigms.cautions: The construction must always emit exactly 14 finite points; avoid parameterizations that merge orbit points at zero radius. The objective is nonsmooth when the identity of a shortest or diameter pair changes, so use a sufficiently large population and do not infer success from a smoothed surrogate alone. A symmetry restriction can miss an asymmetric optimum, so use several independently motivated orbit parameterizations as alternative submitted programs, not sequential optimizations in one call.

tried_paradigms.idea: Use a contact-graph equation solve with scipy.optimize.least_squares to obtain an exact rigid candidate
tried_paradigms.description: The current code already reveals the useful principle: after diameter normalization, the optimum is governed by a small set of active lower-distance contacts and active diameter pairs, while most of its 182 inequalities are slack. Its weakness is that SLSQP repeatedly handles all inequalities and can terminate with small residual violations or an imprecise, slightly asymmetric realization of the same active graph. Build a fixed candidate contact graph from the near-reference configuration: include pairs repeatedly attaining the minimum distance, pairs attaining the diameter, and enough additional contacts to make the framework rigid after fixing translation, rotation, and scale. Parameterize the 14 coordinates in a gauge-fixed form and use scipy.optimize.least_squares once to solve residual equations d_ij^2-u=0 for short contacts and d_ij^2-1=0 for diameter contacts, with optional residuals enforcing intended symmetry. Start from a fixed, hard-coded numerical approximation of the known candidate rather than conducting a preceding optimizer run. After the solve, return the coordinates directly and let the evaluator compute the actual extrema; inactive pairs then certify whether this contact graph is feasible and superior. This attacks numerical error and contact degeneracy rather than merely launching more random full-dimensional searches.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Exact equalization of the distance classes that determine dmin and dmax, thereby improving the true squared ratio and reducing loss from SLSQP feasibility tolerances.
tried_paradigms.cautions: least_squares is an equation solver, not a global maximizer: the selected graph must be independently feasible and rigid, and every noncontact pair must be checked after solving. Fix a complete Euclidean gauge, for example point 0 at the origin, point 1 on the x-axis, point 2 in the xy-plane, plus one diameter normalization, or the Jacobian will be rank deficient. Do not force all near-short pairs to equality if the intended optimum requires some of them to be slack.

tried_paradigms.idea: Directly optimize the normalized max-min objective with scipy.optimize.dual_annealing in gauge-fixed coordinates
tried_paradigms.description: The existing implementation is a hybrid of spherical-code seeding, constrained local SQP, and many incumbent perturbations. This works because spherical repulsion provides well-separated points and analytic constraints make local polishing efficient, but it is biased toward spherical seeds and has no mechanism for accepting a temporary score decrease needed to change the nearest-neighbor graph. Use a gauge-fixed coordinate vector for 14 unrestricted 3D points, with translation removed and a fixed overall box large enough to contain a diameter-one realization. Define one scale-invariant objective as the negative of min(d2)/max(d2), computed from all 91 squared distances, and add deterministic tiny tie-breaking only if needed for numerical stability. Make exactly one scipy.optimize.dual_annealing call with a fixed seed, broad but justified coordinate bounds, high visit parameter, and a local search option using its built-in polishing facility. Unlike the constrained formulation, this has no feasibility boundary: every noncoincident configuration has a valid score, and annealing can cross changes in which pair realizes the diameter or minimum. A successful result can reveal a distinct contact topology; it is then also a source of a fixed candidate for a later equation-based construction, though that later step should be in a separate program variant.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Global improvement of the actual evaluator quantity, including moves that alter both the minimum-distance contact graph and the diameter graph simultaneously.
tried_paradigms.cautions: The ratio is undefined at collapsed configurations, so return a large finite penalty whenever max(d2) is tiny or any value is nonfinite. Bounds should only fix gauge and numerical scale; they must not impose an artificial unit-cube geometric restriction. Full 36-dimensional annealing may be costly, so combine it with a fixed symmetry-aware or gauge-reduced parameterization when timeout is tight, and always use a fixed random seed.
